extracted.intended_audience: members of Parliament, policymakers, and informed public interested in East India Company affairs and colonial finance
extracted.subtask_short: parliamentary speech on East India Company debts
extracted.subtask_description: A parliamentary/historical speech critiquing the legitimacy, accounting, and political consequences of debts claimed by private creditors and the East India Company in India (Carnatic/Nabob of Arcot). Focuses on fraud, usury, concealment, and misapplication of public revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of a debt requires equivalent consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every debt, for which an equivalent of some kind or other is not given, is, on the face of it, a fraud."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid claim must be grounded in a tangible equivalent (goods, services, legitimate advances). Mere assertions of a debt without demonstrable equivalent should be treated as fraudulent. The speaker asks 'What is the equivalent they have given?' and looks for commercial, manufacturing, scientific, artistic, or institutional contributions as possible equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company knowledge and approbation for contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Debts must have been "contracted with the knowledge of the Company" and have their "approbation"; absent that, claims are suspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official authorization and timely notification to the Court of Directors are required. Transactions concealed from the Directors ("it was two years before the Court of Directors obtained any official intelligence of it") indicate breach of duty and undermine the debt's legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assignments of territorial revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Fox's bill contained an express clause "positively forbidding any British subject from receiving assignments upon any part of the territorial revenue, on any pretence whatsoever."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning public/territorial revenues to private creditors is unlawful and a safeguard against rapacity; removal or expunging of such clauses (by later ministry) enabled predatory assignments. Where such prohibitions exist, assignments are improper and claims relying on them should be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: No private advantage at public expense — breach of trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court of Directors condemned servants who "manifestly preferred the interest of private individuals to that of the Company" and accused them of "breach of trust."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents serving a public trust must not use their office to secure private aggrandizement (e.g., acting as creditors/agents for private loans). Evidence of servants acting as both trustees and beneficiaries is a disqualifying conflict of interest and warrants sanction (suspension, dismissal, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of real cash advanced (not mere paper or circular accounting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether "for this debt of 880,000 l. the Nabob ever saw 100,000 l. in real money." The text contrasts 'paper' (teeps/notes) with actual cash advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be supported by proof of real cash disbursements rather than bookkeeping entries, promissory notes, or circular exchanges of bonds. Accounting entries that record non-cash instruments as 'ready money' are an anti-pattern and suggest fraud (the 'soucars' scheme).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usury and capitalization of arrears is illegitimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Interests ranged "from thirty to thirty-six per cent" then were "brought down" and arrears were repeatedly "formed into a new capital" with interest accruing on accumulated sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exorbitant interest rates and the practice of adding unpaid interest to principal (capitalizing arrears) are indicators of predatory, possibly fraudulent, lending. Examination should track original principal versus interest-added capital to determine real indebtedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collusion between debtor and creditors invalidates claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob and his creditors are described as "not adversaries, but collusive parties" and "combining and confederating" against the public revenues and inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where litigation or assignments are the result of collusion among those who appear as debtor and creditor, the transaction should be treated as a scheme to extract public resources. Investigations should test for coordination, mutual benefit, and concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and timeliness of proof to oversight bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The speaker questions when proofs were offered: 'This day, for the first time, we hear of the proofs... But when were these proofs offered?... In what cause? Who were the parties?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private creditors seeking public enforcement must present their evidence promptly and to the appropriate oversight (Court of Directors). Late or belated evidence after public complaints is suspect; oversight bodies have the right to demand timely documentation and to refuse relief absent it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government should not enforce claims that subvert public authority
rubrics_metrics.description: "It was not necessary that the authority of government should interpose in favor of claims whose very foundation was a defiance of that authority, and whose object and end was its entire subversion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state must refuse to back or enforce private arrangements that undermine lawful governance or public interest. Public intervention is inappropriate where claims are founded on acts that seek to subvert or usurp public authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper corporate governance and limits on local presidencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presidency of Madras acted as if it were the Company and "were the very persons guilty of contracting this loan,—creditors themselves, and agents and trustees for all the other creditors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local governance organs must operate within authority delegated by the central Company; assuming creditor/agent roles for private interests violates corporate governance and invalidates transactions made under that usurped authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding public liability for private speculative gain
rubrics_metrics.description: If transactions were "a question between the Nabob of Arcot... and Paul Benfield and his associates, as creditors, I am sure I should give myself but little trouble about it." But because public revenues were involved, Parliament must act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private disputes that do not implicate public funds or administration should remain private; only where actions appropriate affect public revenues or governance should the public treasury or Parliament be asked to intervene or to guarantee claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting and bookkeeping must reflect reality (no false entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice described where bankers 'grants his notes accordingly, which he puts in the cash-book as ready money' though 'not a cash is advanced by the banker.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded 'ready money' entries must correspond to actual cash. Putting notes or commitments into the cash book as cash is fraudulent accounting. Audits should verify physical cash flows, not just ledger entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy consequences of debt on military readiness and public order
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of revenue to satisfy debts left troops unpaid leading to mutiny and desertion: 'One body of troops mutinies for want of pay; a debt is contracted to pay them; and they still remain unpaid... until all the revenues and all the establishments are entangled into one inextricable knot of confusion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims by their effect on public functions (army pay, civil administration). Debts that impair essential services or security are unacceptable and evidence of mismanagement; avoid policies that convert revenue intended for public needs into private claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for servants guilty of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Directors ordered to 'punish, by suspension, degradation, dismission, or otherwise, as to you shall seem meet, all and every such servant or servants of the Company who may ... be found guilty of any of the above offences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigation finds servants guilty of breach of trust or collusive misconduct, formal sanctions including suspension, demotion, dismissal, or prosecution should be applied as deterrence and remedy.
